title: Measuring memorization and copyright risk
bottleneck: Nobody can precisely say how much of a model's output derives from memorized training text versus genuine generalization, because memorization itself lacks an agreed operational definition at scale. This leaves copyright liability unquantifiable: rights holders can't prove derivation, labs can't prove innocence, and courts lack technical standards. Training on the open web makes the problem universal. Saturation is equally corrosive: once scores near 100%, a benchmark stops discriminating between models.
why_it_blocks: Legal uncertainty chills both AI development and creative industries. Without measurement standards, every major model is a lawsuit waiting to happen. Progress claims rest on numbers that conflate memorization, contamination, and genuine capability gains.
current_state: Researchers propose membership-inference and extraction-based metrics, but no standard measure of memorization is accepted by courts or industry.
